title: One Authorisation, One Settlement Form — Northbeam Returns and Restocking
content:
One Northbeam Returns and Restocking authorisation is settled either by refund or by exchange, never by both, and the choice is fixed when the authorisation is settled. Where the customer has taken an exchange and then wants money back instead, the exchange item is returned on its own fresh authorisation under whatever schedule that item falls under, and its window runs from the day the exchange was delivered. A price difference returned on an exchange is not a refund of the line and does not make the authorisation a refund settlement. A price protection claim inside the schedule's price protection days is neither a refund nor an exchange: the difference is returned with the item kept, and it does not use up the return window. Partial quantity settlement follows the same exclusion: the units refunded and the units exchanged are carried on separate authorisations.

## How the exclusion is tested

Whether an authorisation has already taken a replacement rather than money, and what status it stands in, are read from the return authorisation record identified by its own reference number, before it is settled; the customer's expectation of which form they are taking does not settle it. Two settlements on the same authorisation are the case the exclusion forbids, and where an authorisation stands settled the choice made on it is fixed. Where a settlement is properly recorded on that authorisation, it is told apart by the day it was settled and by the way the money went back.

## Three things that are not a refund of the line

| The thing | Why it is not a refund settlement |
| --- | --- |
| a price difference returned on an exchange | it is the difference on the swap, not a refund of the line, and it does not make the authorisation a refund settlement |
| a price protection claim inside the schedule's price protection days | the difference is returned with the item kept; it is neither a refund nor an exchange, and it does not use up the return window |
| a later change of mind about an exchange already taken | the exchange item comes back on its own fresh authorisation, under whatever schedule that item falls under, its window running from the day the exchange was delivered |

## Part of a line

Partial quantity settlement follows the same exclusion. The units refunded and the units exchanged are carried on separate authorisations, never both on one.
